newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: UPS to launch new "Express Plus" service.
newsitem.headline: UPS to launch new "Express Plus" service.

text.p: UPS will be launching a new express service between the U.S. and Europe on March 31.
"Express Plus" enables shipments to be sent from the U.S. to arrive the next day in European Union countries before 08.30 local time in the morning, a UPS spokesman said.
The integrator's new service covers 150 cities and 13 countries in Europe.
In the Netherlands, the major business centres such as Amsterdam, Rotterdam, The Hague, Eindhoven and Schiphol airport are covered by the new service.
UPS' own aircraft fly from the U.S. into its European hub in Cologne and then shipments are trucked to the Netherlands, which is a journey of around four hours, he said.
Express Plus, is a money-back guaranteed service and also UPS said it is a proactive service. The integrator notifies shippers the minute the package is delivered to its final destination, he added.
The company's ordinary express service - UPS Worldwide Express - arrives in Europe before 10.30am and this covers a wider area in the Netherlands.

Last September, UPS launched a service from Europe Union countries to the U.S. which enabled consignments to be delivered before 08.30am but this is limited to the New York and New Jersey area, said the spokesman.
